subject: URGENT: Multi-region gateway 5xx/429 surge — customer impact & exec escalation
messages:
From: Sara Long <ops@acme-retail.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, support@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:03:12 -0500
Subject: Intermittent 502/503/504 + 429 spikes across US/EU/APAC — checkout failing

Diego / Redwood team,

We started seeing intermittent 502/503/504 responses from the Redwood API at ~08:50 ET, and client-side retry logic has amplified the issue — we’re also seeing a sustained 12–18% 429 rate for token-generation calls during peak checkout traffic. Checkout failures are hitting ~3.5% of requests (users are reporting failed transactions). Attached is a short log snippet and a chart from our side showing the spike window (acme_error_rates_chart.png).

Key notes:
- Errors appear simultaneously in US and EU regions; APAC shows a delayed (~+4m) similar pattern.
- Timeouts for the token endpoint are up (p95 -> 2.6s, p99 -> 6.4s)
- Our clients are configured with exponential backoff but short max backoff, so we suspect retry storms amplifying the load.

We need immediate support: production point-of-contact, suggested mitigations, and an ETA to stabilization. Can we hop on a call?

— Sara
Sara Long
Ops, Acme Retail

1) Gather LB/edge metrics (per-region 4xx/5xx, connection queues, retries from proxy).
2) Check for a recent LB/proxy config push (last 6 hours).
3) Consider emergency mitigations: temporary client-side 429 windowing, per-client circuit breaker, restrict concurrency per IP, and routing Acme traffic to dedicated capacity if we can stand it up rapidly.
4) Coordinate an on-call bridge and loop in SRE infra if we need capacity changes.

I’ll reply to Acme with an initial ETA after we have findings.

— Diego Fernandez

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 09:15 AM, diego_fernandez@redwood.com wrote:
> Forwarding Acme report — urgent. Laura / Marcus / Grace, please triage as priority P0.

Quick summary of what I’m seeing from the edge:
- Spike correlates with a rise in client retries hitting the edge (we see a distinct burst pattern in the per-client connection histogram). Looks like a 3x increase in retry attempts in a 2m window.
- EU edge proxies (eu-west-1) show connection queue saturation and >50% of new requests receiving 502s from the LB layer (proxy -> backend timeouts).
- No recent global LB config pushes in the last 8 hours, but we did deploy a small change to prefix caching policy ~+10h ago (low risk) — rolling that back now as precaution.

Actions taken (10:00–10:15):
- Rolled back prefix-caching change to eliminate cache warm-up jobs stepping on thread pools.
- Decreased per-connection keepalive and reduced max concurrent worker threads on edge proxies (hoping to reduce head-of-line blocking).
- Opened a PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-48291

Next steps:
- Marcus to check backend threadpool metrics (KV cache rebuilds, GC), and confirm if Dedicated pool can temporarily take Acme traffic.
- Recommend enabling per-client circuit-breaker and a 30s overall request timeout to reduce backend tail latency exposure.

Laura Bennett
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-gateway-retrystorm-v2.pdf
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:32:47 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 502/503/504 + 429 spikes across US/EU/APAC — checkout failing

Laura / team — findings from backend observability: 
- Backends in us-east-1 are reporting threadpool exhaustion on the token-gen service; GC pauses in a few pods coincide with increased latency and 503s.
- There is a long-running KV cache rebuild job (scheduled) that started around 08:45 ET and amplified CPU contention. That job is being throttled now.
- Connection queuing at the NLB layer is exposing backend timeouts (we see SYN backlog growth).

Mitigations applied (11:20–11:30):
- Increased dedicated pool capacity in us-east by +4 GPUs (hot-standby nodes) and moved Acme traffic to that pool via routing override (temporary).
- Reduced backend request timeout from 45s -> 10s for token-gen paths to fail faster and prevent long tail amplification.
- Applied short-term 429 caching at the edge for repeated token requests to prevent immediate retries.

Proposed immediate options:
A) Keep Acme on dedicated capacity for 24–48h while we fully stabilize.
B) Push client guidance to increase max backoff and jitter (we should send recommended settings).

Marcus Lin
SRE, Serving Runtime

Sara / Raj — summary and next steps from Redwood (apologies for the disruption):

What happened (brief):
- A scheduled KV cache rebuild coincided with a client-side retry surge, producing a retry-storm at the edge and causing backend threadpool exhaustion. The symptoms presented as elevated 502/503/504 and 429 across regions.

What we did (mitigations completed):
- Rolled back a recent prefix-caching policy and throttled the scheduled KV rebuild job.
- Reduced backend timeouts (45s -> 10s) to reduce tail amplification.
- Temporarily routed Acme traffic to dedicated capacity (us-east dedicated pool +4 GPUs) to restore checkout throughput and eliminate cross-tenant interference.
- Enabled short-term 429 caching and per-client circuit-breaker at the edge.

Immediate ask of Acme:
- If possible, increase client backoff max to 30s and add jitter (we’ll share recommended settings) — this will materially reduce retry amplification.
- Confirm if you want us to keep you on the dedicated pool for 24–48h (recommended) — opting in will require a short routing change (done).

Compensation / exec note:
- Grace (cc’d) and I discussed a temporary credit for the incident window; we’ll surface formal credit via your account team.

Follow-ups:
- SRE-runbook updates and a post-incident report will be delivered by EOD tomorrow.
- PagerDuty incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-48291
- We’ve attached the runbook and charts for your review.

If you want, we can run a short bridge now or later this afternoon — please advise.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
